claims.text: Role in encephalitis: don't wait for PCR: start IV acyclovir promptly until HSV and VZV encephalitis are excluded;
claims.quote: Until HSV encephalitis and varicella-zoster virus encephalitis are excluded, intravenous acyclovir should be started promptly

claims.text: continue usually 14 days or until these viruses are excluded;
claims.quote: continued usually for 14 days or until infection with these viruses is excluded

claims.text: can cause LFT abnormalities, marrow suppression and transient renal failure;
claims.quote: Acyclovir is relatively nontoxic but can cause liver function abnormalities, bone marrow suppression, and transient renal failure.

claims.text: giving it IV slowly over 1 h w adequate hydration helps prevent nephrotoxicity.
claims.quote: Giving acyclovir IV slowly over 1 hour with adequate hydration helps prevent nephrotoxicity.

claims.text: Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) dose, herpes simplex encephalitis (adults and adolescents): Adults and adolescents ≥12 y: 10 mg/kg IV infused at a constant rate over 1 h, every 8 h for 10 days.
claims.quote: Adults and Adolescents (12 years of age and older) 10 mg/kg infused at a constant rate over 1 hour, every 8 hours for 10 days.

claims.text: When dosage adjustments are required, base them on estimated CrCl.
claims.quote: When dosage adjustments are required, they should be based on estimated creatinine clearance

claims.text: Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) administration and renal safety: IV infusion only — ⍉ topical, IM, PO, SC, or ocular.
claims.quote: Acyclovir Sodium Injection is intended for intravenous infusion only, and should not be administered topically, intramuscularly, orally, subcutaneously, or in the eye.

claims.text: Infuse over ≥1 h to reduce risk of renal tubular damage.
claims.quote: Intravenous infusions must be given over a period of at least 1 hour to reduce the risk of renal tubular damage

claims.text: Renal failure, in some cases fatal, has been observed w acyclovir therapy.
claims.quote: Renal failure, in some cases resulting in death, has been observed with acyclovir therapy

claims.text: TTP/HUS, which has resulted in death, has occurred in immunocompromised pts receiving acyclovir.
claims.quote: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura/hemolytic uremic syndrome (TTP/HUS), which has resulted in death, has occurred in immunocompromised patients receiving acyclovir therapy.

claims.text: Adequate hydration must accompany IV infusion.
claims.quote: Administration of acyclovir by intravenous infusion must be accompanied by adequate hydration.

claims.text: Other nephrotoxic drugs, pre-existing renal dz, and dehydration make further renal impairment more likely.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of other nephrotoxic drugs, pre-existing renal disease, and dehydration make further renal impairment with acyclovir more likely.

claims.text: Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) CNS effects: ~1% of pts on IV acyclovir show encephalopathic changes (lethargy, obtundation, tremors, confusion, hallucinations, agitation, seizures, coma).
claims.quote: Approximately 1% of patients receiving intravenous acyclovir have manifested encephalopathic changes characterized by either lethargy, obtundation, tremors, confusion, hallucinations, agitation, seizures, or coma.

claims.text: Acyclovir (acyclovir sodium) max dose, CI, interactions, OD: Max dose ≤20 mg/kg every 8 h for any pt.
claims.quote: A maximum dose equivalent to 20 mg/kg every 8 hours should not be exceeded for any patient.

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to acyclovir or valacyclovir.
claims.quote: Acyclovir Sodium Injection is contraindicated for patients who develop hypersensitivity to acyclovir or valacyclovir.

claims.text: Probenecid ↑ acyclovir half-life and AUC; urinary excretion and renal clearance correspondingly reduced.
claims.quote: Coadministration of probenecid with acyclovir has been shown to increase the mean acyclovir half-life and the area under the concentration-time curve. Urinary excretion and renal clearance were correspondingly reduced.

claims.text: OD (ingestions up to 20 g reported): agitation, coma, seizures, lethargy.
claims.quote: Overdoses involving ingestions of up to 20 g have been reported. Adverse events that have been reported in association with overdosage include agitation, coma, seizures, and lethargy.

claims.text: Acute renal failure w anuria may benefit from hemodialysis until renal function restored.
claims.quote: In the event of acute renal failure and anuria, the patient may benefit from hemodialysis until renal function is restored
